questions.text: भू-निम्नीकरण : कृषि योग्य भूमि पर दबाव का कारण केवल सीमित उपलब्धता ही नहीं, वरन इसकी गुणवत्ता में कमी भी इसका कारण है । मृदा अपरदन, लवणता (जलाक्रांतता) तथा भू-क्षारता से भू-निम्नीकरण होता है । भू-उर्वरता के अप्रबंधन के साथ इसके अविरल उपयोग होने पर भू-निम्नीकरण होगा तथा उत्पादकता में कमी आएगी । भू-निम्नीकरण का अभिप्राय स्थायी या अस्थायी तौर पर भूमि की उत्पादकता की कमी है । यद्यपि सभी निम्नकोटि भूमियाँ व्यर्थ भूमि नहीं हैं, लेकिन अनियंत्रित प्रक्रियाएँ इसे व्यर्थ भूमि में परिवर्तित कर देती हैं । भू-निम्नीकरण दो प्रक्रियाओं द्वारा तीव्रता से होता है । ये प्रक्रियाएँ प्राकृतिक तथा मानवजनित हैं । भारतीय दूर-संवेदन संस्थान ने व्यर्थ भूमि को दूर-संवेदन तकनीक की सहायता से सीमांकित किया है और इन प्रक्रियाओं के आधार पर इनको वर्गीकृत किया जा सकता है । जैसे प्राकृतिक खड्ड, मरुस्थलीय या तटीय रेतीली भूमि, बंजर चट्टानी क्षेत्र, तीव्र ढाल वाली भूमि तथा हिमानी क्षेत्र । ये मुख्यत: कारकों द्वारा घटित हुई हैं । इसके अतिरिक्त निम्नकोटि भूमियाँ जैसे जलाक्रांत व दलदली क्षेत्र, लवणता व क्षारता से प्रभावित भूमियाँ, इत्यादि निम्नकोटि भूमियाँ भी हैं जैसे स्थानांतरित कृषि जनित क्षेत्र, रोपण कृषि जनित, क्षरित वन, क्षरित चरागाह तथा खनन व औद्योगिक व्यर्थ क्षेत्र जो मानवीय प्रक्रियाओं से कृषि के अयोग्य हुई हैं ।
questions.text_english: Land Degradation: The pressure on agricultural land increases not only due to the limited availability but also by deterioration of quality of agricultural land. Soil erosion, waterlogging, salinisation and alkalinisation of land lead to land degradation. What happens if land is consistently used without managing its fertility? Land is degraded and productivity declines. Land degradation is generally understood either as a temporary or a permanent decline in productive capacity of the land. Though all degraded land may not be wasteland, but unchecked process of degradation may lead to the conversion to wasteland. There are two processes that induce land degradation. These are natural and created by human beings. National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC) has classified wastelands by using remote sensing techniques and it is possible to categorise these wastelands according to the processes that have created them. There are a few types of wastelands such as gullied/ravinous land, desertic or coastal sands, barren rocky areas, steep sloping land, and glacial areas, which are primarily caused by natural agents. There are other types of degraded lands such as waterlogged and marshy areas, land affected by salinity and alkalinity, which have largely been caused by natural as well as human factors. There are some other types of wastelands such as degraded shifting cultivation area, degraded land under plantation crops, degraded forests, degraded pastures, and mining and industrial wastelands, that are caused by human action.

questions.solution: The three main pillars of human development are Equity, Sustainability, and Productivity. Equity refers to equal access to opportunities for everyone. Sustainability implies the continuity in the availability of opportunities. Productivity refers to human labour productivity.

questions.solution: Three major sources of water pollution in India are the discharge of untreated industrial effluents, agricultural runoff containing fertilizers and pesticides, and the disposal of domestic sewage into water bodies.

questions.text: विश्व में जनसंख्या वितरण को प्रभावित करने वाले किन्हीं पाँच कारकों की विस्तृत व्याख्या कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Explain in detail any five factors affecting the distribution of population in the world.
questions.solution: Population distribution is heavily influenced by several geographical and economic factors. Climate is crucial, as extreme temperatures are unfavorable. Landforms determine settlement patterns; plains are usually densely populated. Availability of water is essential for life and agriculture. Soil fertility attracts agricultural communities, and economic factors like the presence of industries and transport networks facilitate urbanization and population concentration. These five factors collectively shape global demographics.

questions.text: भारत में सड़क परिवहन की किन्हीं पाँच लाभों की व्याख्या कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Explain any five advantages of road transport in India.
questions.solution: Road transport in India offers several advantages. First, it provides door-to-door service. Second, it is highly flexible as routes and timings can be adjusted. Third, it is generally cheaper for short-distance travel. Fourth, it is the primary mode of connectivity for rural and remote areas. Finally, it acts as a feeder service for other transport modes like railways and airways.

questions.text: विश्व में फुटकर व्यापार के किन्हीं पाँच प्रमुख प्रकारों का वर्णन कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Describe any five major types of retail trading in the world.
questions.solution: Major types of retail trading include fixed store retailing, which involves permanent shops. Street peddling, or itinerant trading, involves hawkers selling goods. Consumer cooperatives are run by the people for their own benefit. Mail order businesses allow shopping through catalogues. Finally, automatic vending machines provide convenience for common goods.

questions.text: स्वच्छंद उद्योगों की किन्हीं पाँच मुख्य विशेषताओं का वर्णन कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Describe any five main characteristics of foot-loose industries.
questions.solution: Foot-loose industries possess several distinct characteristics. They are not dependent on specific raw materials. They use components that are produced in small quantities. Their location is primarily determined by access to transport networks. These industries are generally pollution-free. They often involve highly specialized labor and technology, and can be located in diverse settings.

questions.text: भारत में प्रवास के किन्हीं पाँच आर्थिक परिणामों का वर्णन कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Describe any five economic consequences of migration in India.
questions.solution: Migration has significant economic consequences. Remittances sent by migrants improve their families' standard of living. Large-scale migration from rural to urban areas helps provide labor for industrial growth. However, it can also lead to 'brain drain' if skilled workers leave their home regions. Migration contributes positively to the GDP of receiving areas. It also impacts rural development by changing labor availability for agriculture.
